Manifesto/Calibrated Evidence
Principle 01 / optical fidelity

Calibrated Evidence

Measurements should retain their source frame, calibration state, and known uncertainty.

Why it matters

A rule for accountable court intelligence

CourtSpec treats calibration as part of the result, not a hidden setup step. A number without its capture conditions is incomplete.

Production teams should document lens profile, camera position, frame rate, reference geometry, and acceptance tolerance.

A principle becomes a product claim only after representative human and technical validation.

Implementation rules

Operational guardrails

Design rule
Show the evidence chain
Operational rule
Recalibrate when conditions change
Quality rule
Report uncertainty
Governance rule
Do not overstate accuracy
Verification evidence

How the principle is demonstrated

  1. Define the intended coaching decision.
  2. Select a capture setup appropriate to that decision.
  3. Validate against known reference geometry.
  4. Retain calibration metadata with the trace.
